name: Podbean
tagline: Podcast hosting, live streaming, monetization, and distribution

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 5 hours/500 MB total lifetime storage; 100 GB bandwidth/month; 3 episodes/day; 100 MB/file; RSS shows 20 episodes

tiers.name: Unlimited Audio
tiers.limits: 1 podcast; 1 GB uploads/month (about 16 audio hours); unlimited storage; 600 AI credits/month
tiers.notes: The supplied snapshot said $14/month; the live page now shows $17 monthly or $12/month on annual billing.

tiers.name: Unlimited Plus
tiers.limits: 2 audio/video podcasts; 10 GB uploads/month (about 160 audio or 10 video hours); 2,400 AI credits/month

tiers.name: Network
tiers.limits: Unlimited podcasts; 40 GB uploads/month; 3 TB bandwidth/month; 6,000 AI credits; 50 team members

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited private podcasts plus 2 public podcasts; 40 GB uploads/month; 6,000 AI credits; 100 private members

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 hours/500 MB total storage, 100 GB bandwidth/month, 3 episodes/day, 100 MB/file and 20 episodes in the RSS feed
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual rates are billed yearly
pricing.hiddenCosts: Despite the word Unlimited, paid plans cap monthly uploads; extra podcasts and additional AI credits are sold separately at prices not posted publicly.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Podbean's durable value is media pipeline, hosting, distribution, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local podcast hosting workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: recording recovery, mastering, hosting, and distribution
whyPeopleStillPay: Podbean: People pay to avoid codec failures, upload limits, rendering surprises, lost recordings, and distribution chores.
ongoingBurden: Maintain codecs, media probing, resumable processing, storage cleanup, exports, device permissions, and performance.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Podbean Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Five hours total and a 20-episode RSS feed; that is a sample tray, not a home.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Spreaker Free Speech
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The hosting is real, but Spreaker discontinued livestreaming; one of Podbean’s core jobs is gone.

notes: Credibility row: Podbean survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Podbean; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + FFmpeg + React.
Primary job: Build a local podcast hosting workflow that imports user-owned media, applies the core edit or transformation, previews it, and exports a standard file.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: professional codecs, effects, and collaboration; recording recovery, mastering, hosting, and distribution; hosted recording reliability.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
